skill.name: docker-helper
skill.description: Helps generate, optimize, and troubleshoot Dockerfiles and Docker Compose configurations for common application stacks.
skill.summary: Generate and improve Dockerfiles, Compose files, health checks, and container troubleshooting steps.
skill.author: CuriousLearner

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown Dockerfile, Compose, and shell examples rather than executable skill behavior. One hardcoded database password example is confirmed, and the skill also presents destructive Docker cleanup commands without a clear warning.

remediation.issue: Hardcoded database password in Compose example
remediation.suggestion: Replace literal credentials with placeholders or Docker secrets, and show users how to load secrets from a managed source.

remediation.issue: Destructive Docker cleanup commands lack a warning
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear warning before prune commands and recommend checking affected resources before deletion.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Docker Cleanup Command Without Warning
semantic_findings.description: The Docker commands reference includes `docker system prune -a` and `docker volume prune` as cleanup commands. These commands can delete unused images, containers, networks, and volumes, so users need explicit caution before running them.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The commands are clearly present in the Docker reference section and are destructive in normal Docker usage. The surrounding text does not warn about data loss risk.

content.value_statement: Docker setup can be slow, insecure, or hard to debug. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code generate practical container files and troubleshooting guidance.
actual_capabilities: Generates Dockerfile examples for Node.js, Python, and Go applications.
Creates Docker Compose examples for multi-service web, API, database, cache, and proxy stacks.
Suggests multi-stage builds, layer caching, smaller base images, and .dockerignore entries.
Explains common Docker failures such as startup exits, networking issues, and volume permission problems.
Provides health check examples and container command references for local debugging.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not automatic validation of a running Docker environment.
Generated configurations still need review for application-specific ports, secrets, and resource limits.
Some examples use placeholder credentials that should not be copied into production.
It does not replace vulnerability scanning or image signing in a release pipeline.

use_cases.title: Create a first container setup
use_cases.description: Generate a starter Dockerfile and Compose file for a small application with a database and cache.

use_cases.title: Improve build speed and image size
use_cases.description: Review an existing Dockerfile and apply multi-stage builds, better caching, and smaller base images.

use_cases.title: Debug local container failures
use_cases.description: Use structured troubleshooting steps for failed starts, broken service networking, and volume permission errors.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Dockerfile
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new project container file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use docker-helper to create a Dockerfile for my application. Ask me for the language, start command, port, and dependency files first.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Compose stack
prompt_templates.scenario: Build a local multi-service development environment.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use docker-helper to draft a docker-compose.yml for a web app, API, Postgres database, and Redis cache. Include networks, volumes, and health checks.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize an existing Dockerfile
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve performance and security of current container files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use docker-helper to review this Dockerfile for image size, layer caching, non-root execution, health checks, and production readiness.

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot a Compose failure
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced debugging for a broken container stack.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use docker-helper to diagnose why my Compose services cannot connect. Review the service names, networks, depends_on settings, health checks, and logs.

output_examples.input: Generate Docker support for a Node.js API.
output: A multi-stage Dockerfile that installs dependencies before copying source files.
A production stage that runs as a non-root user and exposes the application port.
A health check recommendation and notes for required environment variables.

output_examples.input: Optimize my Dockerfile because builds are slow.
output: A list of cache-breaking steps and how to reorder them.
A recommendation to copy dependency manifests before application code.
Suggestions for .dockerignore entries and smaller base images.

output_examples.input: My API container cannot reach Postgres in Compose.
output: Checks for shared networks and the database service name.
Guidance to use the service name as the host inside Compose.
Health check and startup dependency adjustments to reduce race conditions.

best_practices: Review generated files before use, especially ports, volumes, credentials, and destructive commands.
Use specific base image versions and rebuild images regularly for security updates.
Keep secrets outside images and prefer environment management or secret stores for production.
anti_patterns: Do not copy placeholder passwords from examples into shared or production environments.
Do not run Docker prune commands without checking what resources may be deleted.
Do not rely on this skill as the only security review for production containers.

faq.question: Can this skill generate Docker Compose files?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides Compose examples for multi-service applications with networks, volumes, dependencies, and health checks.

faq.question: Does it support multiple programming languages?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples cover Node.js, Python, and Go, and the patterns can be adapted to other stacks.

faq.question: Can it make images smaller?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends multi-stage builds, smaller base images, cache-friendly layer ordering, and .dockerignore usage.

faq.question: Is it safe for production Docker work?
faq.answer: It is useful for drafting and review, but production files need secret handling, vulnerability scanning, and environment-specific validation.

faq.question: Can it troubleshoot running containers?
faq.answer: It can guide debugging with logs, inspect output, networks, health checks, and service names, but it does not inspect systems by itself.

faq.question: Does it execute Docker commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill contains example commands and guidance. Users should review commands before running them.
